These are two of the first verbs you'll ever need: **to speak** (اتكلم — itkallim) and **to understand** (فهم — fehem). "I speak a little Arabic" and "I don't understand" come up on day one. Tap any sentence to reveal its franco and English.


## How it works

**The present and past you already know:** بـ for the present (*batkallim* = "I speak"), endings for the past (*itkallimt* = "I spoke"). The future is just **ها +** the present stem without بـ: *hatkallim* ("I'll speak"), *hafham* ("I'll understand").

**Understanding likes the participle.** Just like *raye7* / *gayy* from the movement lessons, the verb فهم has an adjective-like form **فاهم (fahim)** that you use for the *state* of understanding right now. "I understand" is far more often **أنا فاهم (ana fahim)** than the full present *bafham*. Its negative, **مش فاهم (mesh fahim)** = "I don't understand", is one of the most useful phrases in the language.

**Two ways to say "not".** With the participle, put مش in front: *mesh fahim*. With the verb itself, wrap it in **ما...ش**: *mabatkallimsh* = "I don't speak", *mafhemtesh* = "I didn't understand".

## Examples

<details class="frase">
<summary>أنا بتكلم عربي شوية</summary>
<span class="fr">ana batkallim 3araby shwayya</span>
<span class="en">I speak a little Arabic</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>أنا فاهم</summary>
<span class="fr">ana fahim</span>
<span class="en">I understand / I get it</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>أنا مش فاهم</summary>
<span class="fr">ana mesh fahim</span>
<span class="en">I don't understand</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>هي بتفهم عربي بس مبتتكلمش</summary>
<span class="fr">heyya bitifham 3araby bas mabtitkallimsh</span>
<span class="en">she understands Arabic but doesn't speak</span>
</details>

## To speak — اتكلم — itkallim

**Root:** ك-ل-م (k-l-m) — reflexive verb. Future: ها + stem (*ana hatkallim, huwwa hayitkallim*).

| Present | Past |
|---|---|
| أنا باتكلم - ana batkallim | أنا اتكلمت - ana itkallimt |
| إنت بتتكلم - inta bititkallim | إنت اتكلمت - inta itkallimt |
| إنتِ بتتكلمي - inti bititkallimi | إنتِ اتكلمتي - inti itkallimti |
| هو بيتكلم - huwwa biyitkallim | هو اتكلم - huwwa itkallim |
| هي بتتكلم - hiyya bititkallim | هي اتكلمت - hiyya itkallimet |
| إحنا بنتكلم - e7na binitkallim | إحنا اتكلمنا - e7na itkallimna |
| إنتو بتتكلموا - intu bititkallimu | إنتو اتكلمتوا - intu itkallimtu |
| هم بيتكلموا - humma biyitkallimu | هم اتكلموا - humma itkallimu |

## To understand — فهم — fehem

**Root:** ف-ه-م (f-h-m) — regular verb. Future: ها + stem (*ana hafham, huwwa hayifham*).

| Present | Past |
|---|---|
| أنا بفهم - ana bafham | أنا فهمت - ana fehemt |
| إنت بتفهم - inta bitifham | إنت فهمت - inta fehemt |
| إنتِ بتفهمي - inti bitifhami | إنتِ فهمتي - inti fehemti |
| هو بيفهم - huwwa biyifham | هو فهم - huwwa fehem |
| هي بتفهم - hiyya bitifham | هي فهمت - hiyya fehmet |
| إحنا بنفهم - e7na binifham | إحنا فهمنا - e7na fehemna |
| إنتو بتفهموا - intu bitifhamu | إنتو فهمتوا - intu fehemtu |
| هم بيفهموا - humma biyifhamu | هم فهموا - humma fehmu |

**Participle of فهم:** فاهم / فاهمة / فاهمين — fahim / fahma / fahmeen — "understanding / I get it" (m. / f. / pl.)

## Languages

| Arabic - franco | English |
|---|---|
| عربي - 3araby | Arabic |
| إنجليزي - engelizi | English |
| فرنساوي - faransawi | French |
| ألماني - almani | German |
| إيطالي - itali | Italian |
| إسباني - esbani | Spanish |
| برتغالي - borto8ali | Portuguese |
| صيني - sini | Chinese |
| لغة / لغات - lo8a / lo8at | language / languages |

## Helper words

| Arabic - franco | English |
|---|---|
| شوية - shwayya | a little |
| كويس - kwayyes | well / good |
| كل حاجة - koll 7aga | everything |
| بسرعة - bisor3a | fast / quickly |
| بالراحة - bera7a | slowly / take it easy |
| تاني - tani | again / another |

## Useful phrases

<details class="frase">
<summary>بتتكلم إنجليزي؟</summary>
<span class="fr">bititkallim engelizi?</span>
<span class="en">Do you speak English?</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>ممكن تتكلم بالراحة؟</summary>
<span class="fr">momken titkallim bera7a?</span>
<span class="en">Can you speak slowly?</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>مش فاهم، ممكن تاني؟</summary>
<span class="fr">mesh fahim, momken tani?</span>
<span class="en">I don't understand — again, please?</span>
</details>

## Dialogue: "Do you speak Arabic?"

Youssef chats with Nour about languages.

<span class="rotulo">يوسف — Youssef</span>
<details class="frase">
<summary>بتتكلمي عربي؟</summary>
<span class="fr">bititkallimi 3araby?</span>
<span class="en">Do you speak Arabic?</span>
</details>

<span class="rotulo">نور — Nour</span>
<details class="frase">
<summary>أيوة، بتكلم شوية</summary>
<span class="fr">aywa, batkallim shwayya</span>
<span class="en">Yes, I speak a little</span>
</details>

<span class="rotulo">يوسف — Youssef</span>
<details class="frase">
<summary>وبتفهمي كل حاجة؟</summary>
<span class="fr">we bitifhami koll 7aga?</span>
<span class="en">And do you understand everything?</span>
</details>

<span class="rotulo">نور — Nour</span>
<details class="frase">
<summary>لأ، بفهم بس لسة مبتكلمش كويس</summary>
<span class="fr">la2, bafham bas lessa mabatkallimsh kwayyes</span>
<span class="en">No — I understand, but I still don't speak well</span>
</details>

<span class="rotulo">يوسف — Youssef</span>
<details class="frase">
<summary>بتتكلمي لغات تانية؟</summary>
<span class="fr">bititkallimi lo8at tanya?</span>
<span class="en">Do you speak other languages?</span>
</details>

<span class="rotulo">نور — Nour</span>
<details class="frase">
<summary>أيوة، بتكلم إنجليزي وفرنساوي</summary>
<span class="fr">aywa, batkallim engelizi we faransawi</span>
<span class="en">Yes, I speak English and French</span>
</details>

### Exercise 3 — Build your own (no answer key)

Say which languages you speak and how well, using **بتكلم + a language + شوية / كويس / نص نص**. Model:

<details class="frase">
<summary>بتكلم برتغالي كويس وعربي شوية</summary>
<span class="fr">batkallim borto8ali kwayyes we 3araby shwayya</span>
<span class="en">I speak Portuguese well and Arabic a little</span>
</details>
